To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the galaxies of the family of isolated galaxies constitute a class of galaxies with particular properties that have evolved independently from the “mainstream” of galaxy population, as a result of the almost total lack of interactions with other galaxies during the last few billions of years.

the family of isolated galaxies is statistically different from the family of perturbed galaxies in size, mass, luminosity, color, morphological type, frequency of barred galaxies, gas content, and FIR/LB ratio, in agreement with the idea that interactions can produce visible effects in the properties of galaxies.

the galaxies in our sample of 203 isolated systems are, in particular: (1) late Spirals, Sc-type; (2) small; (3) low luminosity; (4) low mass; (5) low metallicity; (6) low fraction of barred systems; (7) blue; (8) high specific star formation rate (SSFR); (9) high gas fraction; and (10) high molecular gas fraction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of galaxies outside dense environments.
the characterization of galaxies that are not significantly perturbed by their neighbors.
the characterisation of galaxies in isolation and with the discussion of the origin of their properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the environmental bias is as important as the intrinsic properties of the galaxies in determining the galaxy properties.
a significant fraction of present-day isolated galaxies are late Spiral galaxies derived from high redshift galaxies.
a more “normal” state is that of being perturbed by other galaxies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a strong evidence of evolutionary connection between various stages of the gravitational interaction with other galaxies and the appearance of many field galaxies.

the most important evolution in isolated galaxies occurs through the secular processes of internal formation of disks and bars, mass loss due to stellar and gas stripping, heating of the stellar spheroids, and adhesive inflation due to accretion of cold gas.
the most important structural, photometric and composition features of disk galaxies appear to be related to the environment, particularly to the number of neighbors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
global properties of isolated galaxies are strongly dependent on the method of selection.
the study of isolated galaxies is a very useful approach to understand and clarify the role of interactions in galaxies evolution.
the family of isolated galaxies has properties consistent with those expected for non-evolved, but quietly evolved objects.
